Bug pattern I see constantly: IDOR via object reference in REST APIs.

DELETE /api/orders/1337

Change 1337 to someone else's ID. No ownership check. Full access.

70%+ of apps I scan fail this. Server-side auth on every object. Not optional.

5/ Best lesson from today:
When a UI bug survives multiple fixes, stop tweaking style.
Find out which view actually owns the pixels.
Debug rendering ownership first.
Polish second.
Build in public means sharing the misses too.
#BuildInPublic #ai #llm

2/ The bug wasn’t in the styling.

It was in ownership.

I was polishing the inner rail, but the pixels on screen were actually being drawn by an outer container.

So every “fix” was real…
just applied to the wrong layer.

@antoniogm but is ownership via possession of information vs identity/relationships/laws, a feature or a bug? I use to think it was a feature, but now I feel it’s a bug. I mean maybe in some circumstances it is a good feature for temporary storage, but long term nothing beats peace of mind

Dev vs Prod finally made sense.

In dev:
- loose checks
- errors are fine

In prod:
- real users + data
- security matters
- one bug = real impact

Same code.
But prod needs care, testing, and ownership.
